summary: Continuation of the accepted MC.7 targets: arbitrary-base universal functions, represented degree-Picard points versus actual line-bundle groupoids, their cohomological obstruction and torsor of lifts, fixed-curve infinitesimal points, and six composed consumer contracts. Existing Picard, moduli and upstream targets are imported by their exact owners. Planning completeness is distinguished from native-carrier and supplier-proof closure.

nodes.title: Universal global functions for the level family
nodes.statement: Let f:C→M be the universal smooth projective genus-g curve on the fixed symplectic level component M=M_g[N] over B=Spec Z[1/N,ζ_N]. For every scheme T→M, including non-Noetherian and nonreduced T, the canonical unit O_T→(f_T)_*O_{C_T} is an isomorphism. The identifications for identity and composite base changes agree with the structure-sheaf pullback maps. In particular Γ(C_T,O)^×=Γ(T,O)^× canonically.
hypotheses: g≥2, N≥3; N invertible and a primitive ζ_N fixed.
f is the smooth projective universal family supplied by MC.4; its geometric fibres are connected.
proofSteps: Apply the imported universal-functions statement for prestable curves, or its independent proper-flat-finite-presentation criterion in Stacks Lemma36.32.6. Smooth connected geometric curve fibres are geometrically reduced and connected.

The criterion has no Noetherian-base assumption: its proof uses perfect proper-flat cohomology (Lemma36.32.5) and H⁰(C_s,O)=κ(s) for geometrically reduced connected proper fibres (Lemma33.9.3(7)). Its conclusion already quantifies over all base changes, so it does not merely compare closed fibres.
All maps are the canonical units; naturality of the unit and uniqueness of inverses give identity/composition coherence. Take global sections and units.
acceptance: Specialize to T with nilpotents and to a non-Noetherian affine scheme without adding reducedness or local-Noetherianity.
For a geometrically disconnected proper family the conclusion can fail: two copies of T give O_T×O_T; connectedness is essential.

sources.match: The all-base-change unit isomorphism follows from proper flat finite presentation and geometrically reduced connected fibres.
The existing owner includes universal global functions; this node verifies its use for the level family.

nodes.title: All-base comparison for degree-Picard parameters
nodes.statement: For f:C→M as above and d∈Z, let P=P^d be the degree-d scheme of MC.7/level-picard-parameter and J=P^0. On the big fppf site Sch/M, h_P is naturally the degree-d subsheaf of a_fppf(T↦Pic(C_T)). This is also the sheafification of Pic(C_T)/f_T*Pic(T), with the degree condition imposed on every geometric fibre. P is smooth separated quasi-projective over M, J acts by tensor, and (a,x)↦(x,a·x) identifies J×_M P with P×_M P. Difference is δ(x,y)=y⊗x⁻¹. All these comparisons and actions commute with arbitrary base change, including identity/composition coherence. They make no assertion that P(T) is the pointwise quotient of globally defined line bundles.
hypotheses: Same fixed-component hypotheses as fine-family-functions; d is a fixed integer.
The Noetherian scheme M and its projective smooth connected family satisfy the exact JC0 representability hypotheses.
Degree d is imposed on all components of T; variable locally constant degree belongs to the full disjoint union of components.
proofSteps: Apply the exact JC0 degree and representability nodes to the Noetherian base M. For their proof route, BLR9.3/1 reduces to8.2/1,5 and8.4/2; the supplier audit records the Hilbert/divisor/quotient inputs with their owners rather than replanning them.

A0 gives the two sheafification descriptions and its arbitrary-base-change theorem. A base-changed representing object represents the restricted sheaf by Yoneda, so arbitrary T does not require a new representability theorem over non-Noetherian bases.

For the JC0 torsor, the smooth surjection C→M is an fppf cover and its pullback family has the diagonal section. Its divisor d·Γ (inverse tensor powers for d<0) gives a local degree-d origin. Tensor/difference yield the displayed isomorphism locally; equality and inverses descend in the represented sheaves.
Transfer the already defined tensor, inverse and pullback coherence through representability. Fix the orientation δ(x,y)=y−x so the torsor identity is δ(x,a·x)=a.
acceptance: P^0 has its canonical zero, while P^1 has no chosen origin from this construction. A canonical class of degree2g−2 does not choose a degree-one class.
On T=T₀⊔T₁ a class of degrees0 and1 is not a P^d(T)-point for any single d.
Base change of the action/difference square agrees for two successive morphisms and on dual numbers.

nodes.title: Actual triples and their class morphism
nodes.statement: For a B-scheme T let Trip^d_N(T) be the groupoid of triples (f_T:X→T,η,L): X/T is a smooth projective geometrically connected genus-g curve, η is the fixed-pairing full level N on its Jacobian, and L is an invertible O_X-module of degree d on every geometric fibre. A morphism (X,η,L)→(X′,η′,L′) is a T-isomorphism u:X≅X′ preserving η together with an isomorphism L≅u*L′. Pullback makes a category fibred in groupoids, with its actual tensor/pullback coherence. The functor forgetting L takes values in the fine level moduli groupoid, which is equivalent to the discrete sheaf h_M; sending L to its relative class gives a morphism of fppf stacks q:Trip^d_N→h_P. The fixed-curve fibre is the degree-d full subgroupoid of Core(InvertibleSheaf X), not the full category of module maps and not its set of isomorphism classes.
hypotheses: g≥2,N≥3, chosen ζ_N and exact pairing component; d∈Z.
All morphisms of line bundles in this groupoid are isomorphisms.
Fineness/rigidity of the level curve is imported, not postulated for arbitrary unlevelled curves.
proofSteps: Use the parent fine curve/level groupoid. Attach native invertible sheaves and invertible module maps by the existing line-bundle stack, retaining scalar automorphisms.

Compose isomorphisms with the canonical pullback-composition isomorphism. Pullback of a triple uses the actual cartesian square and the line-bundle pullback of the bundle owner. Degree descent is JC0 through the sheaf comparison.
Curve-family and level descent are parent imports; invertible-module descent is R09.3/SF.1. The class map q is compatible with these data, since relative Picard classes are functorial.

On a fixed X identify the groupoid with the core of the degree-d subcategory; equality of native LineBundleClass is only existence of an isomorphism. No claim that the core itself is discrete follows.
acceptance: Verify each API item and each discriminating test below.
Comparison with h_P is a stack morphism with groupoid-valued source and discrete target; no equivalence is asserted on T.

sources.locator: §8.1 pp.203–205, Picard functor and rigidification discussion
sources.match: Relative classes forget line-bundle automorphisms and base twists.

api.name: actualTriples_pullback
api.statement: For a:T′→T, pull back the curve, level and invertible sheaf; the canonical identity and composite isomorphisms satisfy their cocycle constraints.

api.name: actualTriples_morphism

api.name: actualTriples_relativeClass

api.name: actualTriples_fixedCurveCore

api.name: actualTriples_scalarAut

api.name: actualTriples_tensor

Take genuine fibres of q, with scalar automorphisms and base-change functors, rather than a quotient set.

tests.name: scalar-inertia
tests.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k and a level curve, a fixed L has automorphism group k×. For k=C this group is nontrivial although the corresponding h_P-point has trivial inertia.

tests.name: base-twist
tests.statement: For a fixed level genus-two curve C/C, T=P¹_C and L_T the pullback of a degree-d line bundle L on C, L_T and L_T⊗f_T*O_T(1) are distinct isomorphism classes of triples with the same q-image. Restriction to a constant point of C proves distinctness.

tests.name: noninvertible-map
tests.statement: The zero endomorphism of an invertible sheaf on a nonempty curve is a morphism in the native full module subcategory but is not an arrow of Trip^d_N.

tests.name: tensor-class

nodes.title: The groupoid of lifts of a relative class
nodes.statement: For T→M and p∈P^d(T), define Lift_T(p) as the fibre of q over p: objects are actual invertible sheaves L on C_T whose relative class is p, and arrows are invertible sheaf isomorphisms. Its restriction to Sch/T is fppf locally nonempty and any two objects are fppf locally isomorphic; the automorphism sheaf of any object is canonically G_m,T. Thus it is the G_m-banded gerbe of lifts, with pullback Lift_T(p)|_{T′}≃Lift_{T′}(p|_{T′}). This description asserts the local properties directly and needs no general classification of gerbes by H².
hypotheses: The fixed level family and degree-d component of the preceding nodes.
p is a sheaf point; existence of a global lift is not a hypothesis.
proofSteps: Use the fixed level-family identification to take the genuine groupoid fibre of q, not the fibre of a purported bijection of sets.

Sheafification provides an fppf cover on which p is represented by a line bundle. Equality of two sheafified classes gives local equality of absolute isomorphism classes after refinement, hence local line-bundle isomorphisms.
The automorphism sheaf of a line bundle on C_U is Γ(C_U,O)^× for every U/T; fine-family-functions identifies this with Γ(U,O)^×, compatibly with restriction.
Pullback of line bundles, their isomorphisms and the relative class furnishes the cartesian equivalence with its identity/composition constraints.
acceptance: A nonempty fibre can have many global isomorphism classes and nontrivial inertia; neither property contradicts local isomorphism.
No global Poincaré line bundle is inferred from local nonemptiness.

sources.locator: Lemma108.9.1, tag0DME, proof of local nonemptiness and local isomorphism
sources.match: The gerbe property follows from the definition of the sheafified Picard functor.
Scalars and descent account for the distinction between a relative class and an actual line bundle.

api.name: picardLift_objects
api.statement: An object over U/T is an actual L on C_U together with equality of its relative class with p|_U.

api.name: picardLift_localNonempty
api.statement: Every p has lifts on an fppf cover; any pair of local lifts becomes isomorphic after a further fppf cover.

api.name: picardLift_band
api.statement: For any lift L over U, its automorphism sheaf on Sch/U is G_m,U, naturally in U.

api.name: picardLift_baseChange
api.statement: Restriction along T′→T is equivalent to Lift_{T′}(p|_{T′}); equivalences respect identities and composite pullbacks.

uses.how: Specify the actual lift problem detected by the Leray boundary, without assuming Azumaya or general gerbe-classification theorems.
Separate the local groupoid from its global objects and their isomorphism classes.

tests.name: geometric-field
tests.statement: For algebraically closed k the fibre has an object, every two objects are isomorphic, and its scalar automorphism group is k×; it is equivalent to BG_m(k), not a discrete singleton.

tests.name: pointed-normalization
tests.statement: A section σ:T→C_T gives each p a normalized lift L_norm with σ*L_norm≅O_T, unique up to unique rigidification-preserving isomorphism. Every unnormalized lift is isomorphic to L_norm⊗f_T*N for some base line bundle N. For the constant family over P¹_C, N=O(1) gives a lift not isomorphic to L_norm, although their relative classes agree.

tests.name: base-twist-locality
tests.statement: Over P¹_C, the nonisomorphic lifts differing by O(1) become isomorphic over the standard affine trivializing cover. This tests local isomorphism without global uniqueness.

nodes.title: The obstruction to a global line-bundle lift
nodes.statement: For every T→M there is the functorial exact sequence 0→Pic(T)→Pic(C_T)→Pic_{C_T/T}(T)→H²_fppf(T,G_m)→H²_fppf(C_T,G_m). Its boundary β_T is the Leray differential d₂^{0,1} after identifying f_{T,*}G_m=G_m. For p∈P^d(T), β_T(p)=0 if and only if Lift_T(p) has a global object. Pullback carries β_T(p) to β_{T′}(p|_{T′}). The target is cohomological H², without any identification with Azumaya classes. A section of C_T/T makes β_T zero by the imported splitting; no section of the relative Jacobian is treated as a section of C_T.
hypotheses: Arbitrary T→M; fine-family-functions holds universally for f_T.
Pic means actual line bundles up to isomorphism; the relative Picard term is the fppf sheaf, not a pointwise quotient.
proofSteps: Use the general proper-flat/universal-functions clause of JC4/actual-to-relative-obstruction. The other clauses concerning Pic⁰(J) and autoduality are not prerequisites of this specialization.
Identify f_*G_m with G_m as sheaves on the big fppf base site, using the universal unit isomorphism on every U/T. Identify H¹(G_m) with the Picard group via SF.1.
Read the low-degree Leray sequence with R¹f_*G_m the relative Picard sheaf. Its transgression gives the boundary and its naturality. A0 supplies exactness/injectivity at the earlier terms.
Exactness at the relative Picard term says precisely that p is the class of an actual L. This is global nonemptiness of Lift_T(p), not a chosen lift. For a section use A0/section-picard-split.
acceptance: State every sheaf and cohomology site in the exact sequence and check naturality for arbitrary T′→T.
Zero obstruction yields existence, not a canonical bundle or a trivial automorphism group.
The specialization does not import JC4 autoduality or a section of a Jacobian as a curve section.

sources.locator: §8.1 Proposition4 pp.204–205 and preceding Leray sequence p.203
sources.match: The obstruction is the low-degree cohomological boundary under universal global functions.

nodes.title: Picard torsor of global lifts
nodes.statement: For p∈P^d(T), let LiftClasses_T(p)={a∈Pic(C_T): a maps to p}. This is the set of isomorphism classes of Lift_T(p). Pic(T) acts by n·a=a⊗f_T*n. The action is free, and for any a,b in the fibre there is a unique n with n·a=b. Therefore the fibre is empty exactly when β_T(p)≠0; when β_T(p)=0 it is a Pic(T)-torsor, with no chosen origin. A chosen actual lift L₀ gives a groupoid equivalence Lines(T)→Lift_T(p), N↦L₀⊗f_T*N, as well as a Pic(T)-equivariant bijection Pic(T)→LiftClasses_T(p). These statements are natural for pullback of a specified L₀. Lines(T) means the groupoid Core(InvertibleSheaf T).
hypotheses: Arbitrary T→M, p∈P^d(T).
The torsor assertion includes nonemptiness precisely under β_T(p)=0; the unpointed fibre is not made into a group.
proofSteps: Tensor by a pullback line bundle does not change the sheafified relative class, so it defines the action. The kernel theorem gives injectivity of f_T*:Pic(T)→Pic(C_T), hence freeness.
For two classes a,b in the fibre, b⊗a⁻¹ lies in the kernel. A0 identifies it with a unique class from Pic(T), giving transitivity and the unique difference in the stated orientation.

For a chosen L₀, tensor/pullback gives the displayed functor on actual line bundles. Essential surjectivity follows from the same kernel descent. Full faithfulness uses descent of homomorphisms between pullback invertible sheaves: locally trivialize N,N′ and apply O_T≅f_*O_C; the Hom sheaves and their invertible sections then agree.

Tensor associativity, pullback monoidality and their coherence belong to the bundle owner. They give equivariance, the change-of-origin translation formula, and compatibility with successive base changes.
acceptance: Do not confuse this Pic(T)-torsor of lifts with the J_T-torsor P^d_T of relative degree-d classes.
A global lift changes the entire groupoid to Lines(T), not to a discrete copy of Pic(T).

sources.match: Kernel and scalar descent give the ambiguity of a global representative by a line bundle from the base.
Local equality of lifts retains their invertible-sheaf isomorphisms.

api.name: liftClasses_action

api.name: liftClasses_difference
api.statement: For a,b in one fibre there is exactly one n∈Pic(T) such that b=a⊗f_T*n.

api.name: liftClasses_nonempty

api.name: liftClasses_chooseOrigin
api.statement: A specified lift L₀ identifies Pic(T) equivariantly with LiftClasses_T(p); the origin maps satisfy Φ_{L₀⊗f_T*N}([M])=Φ_{L₀}([N]+[M]), so a fixed lift has new coordinate equal to its old coordinate minus [N].

tests.name: nontrivial-base-Picard
tests.statement: For C/C a fixed level genus-two curve, T=P¹_C and a pullback L₀, the lifts L₀⊗f*O(n) are pairwise nonisomorphic for n∈Z. They all map to one p; the difference between n and m is O(m−n).

tests.name: field-scalar
tests.statement: For T=Spec k with k algebraically closed, Pic(T)=0, so the lift-class fibre is a singleton, while the actual lift groupoid has automorphism group k×.

tests.name: section-normalization
tests.statement: For the same constant family with a constant section σ, all L₀⊗f*O(n) have the same normalized representative. Their σ-rigidified normalized objects are uniquely isomorphic.

tests.name: empty-fibre-convention
tests.statement: The theorem is conditional on β=0 for nonemptiness: an empty fibre with β≠0 is never assigned a torsor structure with an inhabited carrier.

nodes.title: Fixed-curve infinitesimal Picard points
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed with N invertible, C/k a fixed smooth projective geometrically connected genus-g≥2 curve with fixed full level, and L₀ an actual degree-d line bundle. Put A=k[ε]/(ε²), C_A=C×Spec A. The fibre of P^d_C(A)→P^d_C(k) over [L₀] is canonically, using the constant lift of L₀ as origin, the additive k-vector space H¹(C,O_C), of dimension g. It is also the set of isomorphism classes of pairs (L,φ), where L is a line bundle on C_A and φ:L|_C≅L₀, and arrows respect φ. Each framed object has automorphism group 1+εk≅(k,+). Thus a fixed geometric point can have many infinitesimal lifts even though Pic(Spec A)=0. Curve, level and special-fibre bundle stay fixed; this does not compute the tangent space of the full varying-curve stack.
hypotheses: Algebraically closed k; fixed curve C, fixed level η, actual L₀ and its constant pullback.
The JC6 Lie theorem is applied with integral Noetherian base Spec k, not with nonreduced base Spec A.
proofSteps: Tensor by the inverse of the constant lift of L₀ identifies the degree-d reduction fibre with the infinitesimal kernel at zero in J_C. Apply JC6 at Spec k and its dual-number definition of Lie to identify this with H¹(C,O_C).

Concretely 1+εO_C is additively O_C and the split reduction sequence of units identifies the kernel of Pic(C_A)→Pic(C) with H¹(C,O_C). Constants lift all units, so a chosen reduction framing does not change the set of isomorphism classes.

C has a k-point, giving a constant section over A. The A0 pointed splitting identifies relative classes with absolute classes modulo Pic(A), and Pic(A)=0 because A is local. This relates the actual framed problem to P^d_C(A), without applying an integral-base theorem to Spec A.
Framed automorphisms are units reducing to1: by universal functions these are exactly1+εk. Genus gives dim_k H¹(C,O_C)=g from the existing coherent-curve owner.
acceptance: For genus2 the reduction fibre is a two-dimensional k-vector space and is not a singleton.
The constant deformation is zero and adding a class means tensoring its infinitesimal line bundle.
Changing a reduction framing is absorbable by a constant scalar, but scalar units reducing to1 remain automorphisms.

sources.match: The dual-number unit sequence identifies the Lie algebra of the Picard functor with H¹ of the structure sheaf.
The Lie/cohomology comparison is the algebraic input used for the Hodge comparison, with an integral Noetherian original base.

nodes.title: Curve-family export for symplectic L-functions
nodes.statement: For each g≥2, the smooth unpointed curve stack M_g and its universal smooth projective family, after base change to Z[1/|G|] for G=Sp_{2r}(F_ℓ) as in Abdurrahman–Venkatesh, supply the curve-family base of their §5.1 Hurwitz problem. For every T-point h of that Hurwitz stack, the underlying curve is the pullback of the universal M_g-curve along its forgetful map h→M_g. This identification is cartesian and coherent under arbitrary base change; it retains the category-valued curve automorphisms before any level is added.
hypotheses: g≥2 for this unpointed stable-range export.
Fix r≥1 and a finite field F_ℓ of odd cardinality, as in the consumer; invert |Sp_{2r}(F_ℓ)| on the curve-moduli base.
The consumer supplies its own connected-fibre G-cover problem, cyclotomic twist and forgetful morphism.
proofSteps: Apply the parent universal property to the underlying smooth proper curve family in the Hurwitz object. Over a scheme the curve is projective by the genus≥2 canonical-polarization input of MC.0/MC.1.

Base change the universal curve along the consumer forgetful morphism to obtain the same curve over its Hurwitz groupoid. The cartesian equivalence is the classifying-family equivalence, natural on arrows as well as objects.

The central deck transformations, connected-cover condition, possible failure of étaleness of the Hurwitz forgetful map, cyclotomic multiplier and symplectic local system are defined by SymplecticLFunctionsModSquares. They are not consequences of the curve fine-level scheme.
acceptance: Over a test scheme and after a second pullback the classifying curve is canonically the same family.
A central deck automorphism in AV Example5.1 is not removed by replacing the consumer stack with a curve full-level scheme.
No assertion of an unmarked genus-one DM stack or étaleness of the Hurwitz map is made.

sources.match: The argument uses a universal curve over a Hurwitz groupoid, with central cover automorphisms still present.

nodes.title: Pointed stable-stack export for tautological operations
nodes.statement: For all ordered stable pairs (g,n) with 2g−2+n>0, the parent supplies the smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack M̄_g,n/Z of relative dimension3g−3+n, its dense smooth-curve open M_g,n and universal stable family, relabelling of the n ordered marks, forget-and-stabilize, and separating/nonseparating clutching. The normalization of the reduced total boundary is the finite disjoint union of the one-edge vertex-product quotient stacks, retaining the constant finite graph-automorphism groups. After base change to C or to the relevant étale-cohomology base these maps and their coherent compositions are the geometric input of Canning–Larson–Payne §2.1.
hypotheses: Stable pairs, with marks ordered, disjoint and in the smooth locus of each curve.
The consumer supplies Chow/cohomology theories, graph invariants and their push-pull formalism.

nodes.title: Elliptic-stack and coarse-scheme comparison
nodes.statement: For every coefficient field k, the smooth one-pointed genus-one stack M_1,1,k of the parent is equivalent to the elliptic-curve stack Ell/k of current ModularCurves4A–4B, compatibly with the marked universal curve and arbitrary base change. Its coarse algebraic space is therefore canonically the existing coarse j-line A¹_k=Spec k[j] of ModularCurves9E. The comparison is characterized by the coarse classifying maps. It supplies Chen’s elliptic stack and its distinct coarse scheme M(1), without putting a universal elliptic curve on the coarse scheme.
hypotheses: The one mark is a section; smooth proper geometric genus-one fibres.

Import current ModularCurves1C,1D,2D,4A,4B,9D,9E and the exact R09.5 elliptic/coarse-j recovery nodes. The SF.1 finite-quotient-coarse bridge supplies universality among algebraic spaces; the scheme-target universal property of upstream CoarseModuliData alone does not.
proofSteps: Use ModularCurves1C for the pointed Weierstrass presentation and 1D for the canonical scheme-level group law, including arbitrary-base-change compatibility. Use 2D (KM2.5.1, isGroupHom_of_mapsZero) to show pointed isomorphisms preserve that law and to prove uniqueness of a compatible group structure. Forgetting the group law while retaining the identity section is then quasi-inverse to this construction, naturally under base change.
The marked family is identified with the elliptic universal family by the classifying equivalence, not by a coarse-point bijection.

Use R09.5/elliptic-coarse-recovery: the full level3 rigidifier on D(3) and level4 rigidifier on D(2) give the quotient-stack charts imported from ModularCurves4C/9D. SF.1/finite-quotient-coarse upgrades their invariant quotients to coarse spaces universal for algebraic-space targets. The unique comparisons glue on overlaps. R09.5/coarse-j-line-recovery then identifies this coarse space with the coefficient-ring j-line already owned by9E, including its explicit characteristic2/3 results. Transport through the stack equivalence and use MC.4/coarse uniqueness. This proves the latter is a scheme; scheme-target universality alone would not justify the comparison.
No proof of coarse-j representability or its invariant-ring computations is added here. Hurwitz/Nielsen/Higman/Markoff constructions remain in InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.5.
acceptance: Over k of characteristic2 or3 use the coefficient-ring9E theorem, not commutation of arbitrary coarse-space formation with base change.
The stack retains automorphisms of elliptic curves with a marked identity, whereas the j-line is a scheme.
A map to the j-line does not provide a universal elliptic family; the universal curve belongs to M_1,1.

nodes.title: Fine-level and Picard export for DGH
nodes.statement: Fix g≥2,N≥3 and a primitive Nth root over Q̄. On the corresponding exact symplectic component, M_g[N] is a regular geometrically irreducible quasi-projective variety of dimension3g−3 with a universal smooth projective curve f:C→M. The Torelli map τ:M→A_g[N] uses the same level and pairing, and Jac(C/M)≅τ*U_g as principally polarized abelian schemes with level; this is the cartesian square (6.1). The smooth Torelli map has finite geometric fibres (at most two), not an asserted globally finite morphism. The section-free Abel map a₁:C→P¹ and the difference map P¹×_M P¹→J are defined without a section of f and commute with every base change. These compose the moduli/Picard interface used in DGH §6.1.
hypotheses: Characteristic zero, fixed exact pairing component, g≥2,N≥3.
The ppav fine scheme/universal family, principal polarization and strong-Torelli input are the exact suppliers of MC.6.
proofSteps: Choose the pairing component on both curve and ppav moduli before applying the fine universal properties. Smoothness and connectedness from the separate MC.4 nodes imply geometric irreducibility; regularity/quasi-projectivity and dimension come from fineness.

MC.6/smooth-torelli, with its existing ppav and Jacobian suppliers, identifies the actual pulled-back abelian family with Jac(C/M). Yoneda gives the square on arbitrary test schemes, not only on Q̄-points.

Use MC.6/torelli-finite-fibres with its sign qualification. In genus2 all curves are hyperelliptic and the map is injective on geometric points; in the nonhyperelliptic range the two signs can be distinct.

Specialize the JC2 diagonal-divisor Abel map to the universal family and the already imported JC0 torsor difference to P¹. The orientation is a₁(y)−a₁(x). JC5/JC7 own the universal Faltings–Zhang tuple, so that construction is not repeated here.
acceptance: The Jacobian square commutes after dual-number base change and identifies the same principal polarization and level, rather than merely isomorphic geometric fibres.
The construction uses P¹ before choosing a degree-one origin; a curve section is not supplied by the identity section of J.
Preserve finite-to-one versus finite, and check genus2 separately from nonhyperelliptic curves.

sources.match: The exact inputs are regular irreducible level moduli, the cartesian Jacobian square, finite-to-one Torelli, and the section-free Pic¹ difference construction.

nodes.title: Pointed-family export for canonical representations
nodes.statement: For a stable pair (g,n), let B be a connected complex variety and π:C→B a smooth proper genus-g curve with n ordered pairwise disjoint sections. Its classifying morphism B→M_g,n,C is characterized by a cartesian equivalence of the marked family with the universal family, naturally under scheme base change. The consumer’s versality condition is exactly that this morphism is dominant and étale. Neither existence of such a presentation for every family nor versality of an arbitrary family is asserted.
hypotheses: 2g−2+n>0; B a connected complex variety; sections disjoint.
The base letter B here denotes the consumer variety, not the fixed cyclotomic base of the unpointed level convention.
proofSteps: Restrict the parent stable pointed stack and universal curve to their smooth open and base change to C. Apply the classifying property to the actual ordered sections.

The cartesian equivalence is natural on marked-curve isomorphisms and all scheme pullbacks. Express the consumer’s dominant-étale predicate on this classifying morphism without deriving it from smoothness of π.

MappingClassGroupsAndCanonicalRepresentations owns removal of the section divisor, the punctured family, dominant étale charts used in its arguments, analytification, stack fundamental groups and mapping-class identifications. The coarse space cannot replace this stack in those constructions.
acceptance: The constant family with (g,n)=(0,4) over a positive-dimensional B has a classifying map to a point of M_0,4, hence is not versal.
The ordered sections and their labels survive the classifying equivalence; permutation is a specified operation.
Unmarked genus1 is outside the stable range; marked genus1 and stable genus0 pairs are included.

nodes.title: Stable, level and Picard export for Yuan
nodes.statement: For g>1 the smooth/stable curve stacks and universal families of MC.0–MC.2, together with their separate coarse schemes from MC.4 (projective for the stable unpointed space), supply Yuan §3.1.1. On each fixed symplectic level component with N≥3 invertible, the fine smooth scheme and the stable extension after a finite dominant cover are the MC.4/MC.6 exports used in the fine-level compactification discussion. For degree-d triples in §4.3.2, fix ζ_N over an algebraically closed field k. Yuan permits symplectic similitude multiplier c∈(Z/N)×; his parameter is therefore the finite disjoint union P^d_sim=⊔_c P^d_c, not just the exact c=1 component. Precomposition by diag(c⁻¹I_g,I_g) identifies the c-component with the exact component; precomposition by diag(cI_g,I_g) is the inverse. For every algebraically closed extension F/k, P^d_sim(F) is bijective to isomorphism classes of Yuan’s actual degree-d level-N triples over F. For a general T, use q and its obstruction/torsor of lifts instead. The algebraic Lie/Hodge comparison in Lemma3.4 is imported on its integral Noetherian stable-family bases; its metric assertion is outside this export.
hypotheses: g>1; in the level/Picard clause, N≥3 invertible and primitive ζ_N fixed.
The stable extension is after the cover/normalization of MC.6; no moduli interpretation by naive nodal full torsion frames is used.
For Lemma3.4 the original base is integral Noetherian; geometric constant-field conventions in §4.3.2 use the chosen embedding k̄→K̄.
proofSteps: Compose the smooth/stable stack universal properties with their coarse classifying maps, keeping the universal family on the stack. MC.4/projective-coarse makes the stable unpointed coarse algebraic space a projective scheme. Its smooth-curve open is the smooth coarse scheme, using coarse restriction under open (hence flat) base change. Apply the exact finite-cover stable-compactification export on each smooth level component; stable boundary existence is a parent supplier, not inferred from the Picard scheme.

For a frame η with e(ηv,ηw)=ζ_N^{c⟨v,w⟩}, precompose η with diag(c⁻¹I_g,I_g) to obtain an exact frame; the inverse precomposition gives multiplier c. This works over any base with ζ_N and separates the finitely many constant multiplier components. Apply the same change of frame to the pulled-back universal curves and degree-Picard schemes.

For F algebraically closed, use the existing parent geometric-point comparison on each component. Its surjectivity follows by finding an F-point in an fppf cover carrying a lift; uniqueness of the line-bundle class uses Pic(F)=0. Scalar automorphisms remain in the triple groupoid. Disjoint union gives the stated similitude comparison.

For arbitrary T apply the exact obstruction and lift-torsor nodes. For Lemma3.4, use JC6 Lie(J/S)≅R¹π_*O and stable-curve duality to obtain π_*ω≅e*Ω¹_J/S and then its determinant. MC.5 owns determinant formation, MC.6 owns the smooth universal comparison; metric compatibility remains the arithmetic/analytic consumer’s work.

The routed Picard item requires the geometric triple comparison, not a new proof of Lemma4.8 or a rational-field isotriviality criterion. Do not infer descent of an actual line bundle to a smaller nonclosed field from descent of its sheaf class.
acceptance: For N=3 there are two multiplier components c=1,2; the exact component alone does not parametrize all the permitted frames.
Over algebraically closed F the lift-class fibre is a singleton with scalar inertia F×; over T=P¹_C the base-twist test refutes the unqualified global-bundle interpretation.
In a one-variable function-field application read the bars in k̄ and K̄ geometrically; no rational-field descent theorem is smuggled into the geometric-point bijection.
The stable family lies over the covering compactification, and the boundary is not claimed to carry ordinary full N-torsion of an abelian Jacobian.
The determinant Hodge line λ and the rank-g Hodge vector bundle E have distinct types.

For a fixed relative polarization H, a degree-d line has polynomial d+n deg(H)+1−g. A uniform twist makes degree at least2g+1, so fibre Riemann–Roch and duality give H¹=0 and global generation. Relative cohomology/base change then gives the same finite-rank pushforward on all tests. Nonzero fibre sections then cut relative effective Cartier divisors; their parameter fibres are projective spaces, not finite sets.
supplierProofAudit.proofClosure: R09.2 supplies fixed-polynomial Hilbert/Quot on all tests; R09.3 supplies descent of quasicoherent ideals/invertible modules. BLR8.2/12 classifies equivalence classes by their Hilbert points, descends the graph to a closed Hilbert locus, and yields the proper faithfully flat quotient and quasi-projectivity. This generic proper-flat quotient is not supplied by the existing finite-locally-free quotient comparison. A precise R09.3 request below records that target; the curve Picard theorem itself is already planned by JC0.

In this curve case fixed-degree boundedness follows from the uniform twist and the resulting finite-rank evaluation quotient; the full higher-dimensional boundedness assertions of BLR8.2/13,14 are unnecessary.
